**Reasoning as this farmer:**

My family has worked this land in Quzhou for three generations. I have about 10 mu total. I didn't go to school but I know this land — my father showed me, and I watch what the neighbors do. The grain purchasing station always buys wheat and corn, so that's what I grow. Nobody around here grows anything else on the main fields.

Most of my 9 mu I'll do wheat-corn rotation, same as always. Plant wheat in October after corn comes off, harvest it in June, then put corn in right away on the same ground. The 1 mu near the house I keep for garlic and vegetables — my wife handles that mostly, we eat it and sell some at the township market.

For wheat seed I'll buy from the village ag supply store — they sell the improved Jimai variety, everyone uses it, yields are decent. For corn I'll get Zhengdan 958 hybrid, that's what my brother-in-law uses and he does well with it.

Fertilizer: I put down compound fertilizer (15-15-15) before wheat planting, then urea when it starts jointing in spring. Same approach my father used, just with the chemical bags now instead of manure. Maybe I use a bit more urea than I should but I don't want the crop to turn yellow.

Irrigation: we pump from the village well. Wheat needs water four times — once before planting in October to settle the seed, once in December before it freezes, once in March when it joints, once before it heads. Corn only needs one or two waterings if summer rains are light.

I use the rotary tiller to prepare wheat ground. For corn I don't plow — I just seed right into the stubble with the seeder, saves money and time.

For pesticides, wheat gets herbicide in winter and then I spray something for aphids and mildew in spring. Corn I spray herbicide after seeding and watch for the borer in July.

I expect about 450 jin per mu on wheat, maybe 550 on corn. Same as last year if weather cooperates.
